transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. I'm here because I've been having a really hard time staying focused and paying attention to my tasks lately. It has gotten to the point where it is starting to seriously impact my daily life.
When did you first start having trouble with focus and attention—was it something that began in childhood or more recently in adulthood?
It definitely started back in childhood, well before I turned 12. However, this current stretch of really struggling to focus has been going on consistently for about a year and three months now.

{
  "category": "differential point",
  "subcategory": "symptom persistence",
  "question": "Have you had ongoing difficulties with attention and focus throughout your life, or were there periods where you didn’t experience these problems?"

I would say it has always been there in the background since I was a kid, though there were times with more structure where it felt a bit more manageable. It never completely went away, but it has definitely become much more constant and harder to handle recently.

{
  "category": "differential point",
  "subcategory": "functional impairment",
  "question": "In what ways has the difficulty with focus been affecting your work, relationships, or daily responsibilities?"

It's really impacting my daily responsibilities because I'm constantly forgetting important things, like paying my bills on time, keeping appointments, and running errands. I also struggle a lot with organizing my tasks and activities, which makes it feel almost impossible to manage my day-to-day life.

{
  "category": "differential point",
  "subcategory": "symptom specificity",
  "question": "Do you also find it difficult to stay focused when reading, listening in conversations, or during meetings, even when you want to pay attention?"

Yes, absolutely. Even when I am trying my absolute best to pay attention, my mind constantly drifts off during meetings or when people are talking directly to me. Reading is also a major struggle because I often have to re-read the same page multiple times just to process it.

{
  "category": "differential point",
  "subcategory": "symptom severity and pervasiveness",
  "question": "Do these focus difficulties happen in multiple settings, such as at home, at work, and in social situations, or are they mostly limited to one area of your life?"

Yes, they definitely happen across multiple areas of my life, both at home and in my daily social life. At home, I struggle to keep up with chores and constantly forget to pay my bills on time. In my daily life, I'm always forgetting to run errands, return phone calls, or keep appointments that I've made.

The patient reports childhood onset of inattention (before age 12), persistent symptoms across the lifespan with increased severity recently, and clear functional impairment in multiple domains (home, work, social). The core symptoms of difficulty sustaining attention, forgetfulness, poor organization, and mind wandering during conversations or reading align with DSM-5 criteria for this presentation. No symptoms of hyperactivity/impulsivity were reported, and there is no evidence of mood, anxiety, trauma-related, or psychotic disorders that would support an alternative diagnosis. Thus, the candidate list remains unchanged.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a lifelong pattern of inattention symptoms beginning in childhood, with persistent difficulties in focus, organization, and task completion that are pervasive across multiple settings (home, work, social). Key symptoms include mind drifting during conversations, frequent forgetfulness, difficulty following through on tasks, and needing to re-read material, all consistent with predominantly inattentive ADHD.
